Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
As the Carte Blanche Making a Difference Trust is announced the recipient of 2023's POP Classic concert, we reflect on a decade and a half spent working to improve healthcare for South Africa's most v

Unique Selling Point:
Carte Blanche's Making a Difference Trust has a unique legacy in South Africa: a television programme that has raised millions to improve paediatric healthcare facilities in government hospitals. What started as a project to celebrate the programme's 20th birthday is going strong 15 years later, and continues to draw vital funding for the never-ending list of projects it tackles each year.

Further information:
Lexus POP Classics 2023 will take place on 22 July 2023 in association with Laeveld Agrochem, Virseker, kykNET and Belgravia Gin, at the SunBet Arena for one night only!

Demi Lee Moore, Samantha Leonard, Tarryn Lamb, Ruhan du Toit, Monique Steyn, Corlea, Timothy Moloi, Boki, Amira Willighagen and the Mzansi Youth Choir, performing hits by Miley Cyrus, Adele, Queen, The Beatles, Whitney Houston, Joni Mitchell, Lady Gaga, Meatloaf, Bruce Springsteen, Celine Dion and many more.

Script:


VOICE OVER: For three decades, South Africans have trusted Carte Blanche to bring them the truth.
But in 2008 – our 20th Birthday – we went beyond journalism. Moved by equipment shortages and crumbling infrastructure in our public hospitals, we established the Carte Blanche Making a Difference Trust. George Mazarakis was then Executive Producer.

UPSOUND: George Mazarakis: It was heart-wrenching to see these people working in really abject conditions and children not making it, not surviving, because the hospital didn’t have what it needed to look after them properly.

VOICEOVER: The goal was simple: to improve conditions for children in critical care facilities, from ICUs to Burn Units. But the Trust has grown beyond what Patron Karolina Andropoulos could ever have imagined.

UPSOUND: Karolina Andropoulos: There are moments where all this seems overwhelming and other moments where anything is possible. […] The campaign is the success it is because of the spirit of generosity.

VOICE OVER: In 15 years, the Trust has saved the lives of thousands of children in over 20 hospital projects, from Tygerberg in Cape Town… to Ngwelezana in rural KwaZulu Natal.

UPSOUND: Dr Henk Kruger: We now work in a first world hospital in a third world setting.

VOICE OVER: We’ve changed the story for children like Innocentia, relying on Sebokeng Hospital for lifelong diabetes treatment...and Yolanda, who accessed specialist surgery at Frere Hospital.

UPSOUND: Yolanda’s mom: I am very happy because life will be better for her.

VOICE OVER: They inspire our mandate: to ensure that illness and injury do not cripple the future of our country’s most vulnerable. Their need has not diminished. With the support of viewers, donors and partners, the Carte Blanche Trust will continue to make excellent healthcare available to every child in every part of South Africa.
